caption:
The AI gave the sticky header a frosted-glass blur. Now the mobile menu opens inside a 64px strip instead of covering the screen.

Look at the card. position: fixed usually means "relative to the viewport". But when an ancestor has backdrop-filter, filter or transform, that ancestor becomes the containing block. inset: 0 now means "fill the header", and the header is 64px tall.

Move the drawer out of the header so it's a sibling, and fixed is relative to the viewport again. In React, a portal to document.body does the same.

Modals inside animated cards break the same way.

Source: MDN, Containing block (identifying the containing block).
